newsitem.title: UK: POLL-British rates seen rising to 6.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-British rates seen rising to 6.75 pct.

text.p: The Bank of England's monetary policy committee is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its meeting this week, a survey showed on Tuesday.

Financial analysts 4CAST said that in a poll of 75 contributors from dealing desks across Europe, 61 predicted rates would increase to 6.75 percent from 6.50 percent. Six saw a rise of 50 basis points and eight forecast no change.

The Bank of England's monetary policy committee begins its two-day meeting at 1400 GMT on Wednesday and will announce its decision on interest rates at 1100 GMT on Thursday, a central bank official said.

The 4CAST poll, conducted on Monday, is in line with a Reuters survey of financial analysts carried out last Thursday. In the Reuters poll, 17 out of 24 responses predicted a 0.25 percentage point rise, and four forecast an increase to seven percent.
Analysts said a rise in interest rates was widely expected because last week's budget had not done enough to quell consumer spending and contain the overheating economy.

The 4CAST survey showed that expectations for sterling varied widely, with a rise of 25 basis points giving a range of predictions for the pound at close of business on Friday between 2.88 and 3.00 marks, with a median forecast of 2.94 marks.
Sterling was trading at 2.9720 marks at 0840 GMT on Tuesday.

Assuming a rise in interest rates to seven percent, predictions for sterling ranged between 2.8675 and 3.05 marks, with a median forecast of 2.9750 marks. And if there were no change to interest rates, the median forecast was 2.90 marks.
